conviction_note: Two things I found are genuinely fresh and both point up - Palo Alto's identical July-quarter SASE bookings +40% published one session ago with NTSK's tape flat, and the Q1 10-Q line items showing the free-cash-flow collapse that caused the -19% was an accounts-receivable collection comp ($22.1M vs $79.7M) rather than structural burn - but both agree with the call-bid skew and the +28% recovery off the June low, so most of it is already in the price; I net them against a 0-for-3 print base rate and post-lockup float supply and land only marginally above zero versus a 17.8% implied move.

findings.finding: Netskope's Q1 FY27 cash flow statement shows the free-cash-flow reversal that produced the -19% June print was overwhelmingly working capital, not spending: the accounts-receivable collection tailwind shrank to $22.1M from $79.7M a year earlier, accrued compensation drained $43.6M vs $26.5M and deferred revenue $23.0M vs $4.7M - together more than the entire $79.5M year-on-year swing in operating cash flow (-$53.9M vs +$25.6M) - while the non-GAAP operating loss margin was roughly flat at -14.5%, and the fiscal Q2 comp carries no post-year-end collections distortion.
findings.why_not_priced: The three sell-side actions I can find in August (RBC $13 to $18 on 08-14, Wells $13 to $17 on 08-17, Oppenheimer $16 to $19 on 08-19, against a Deutsche Bank downgrade to Hold on valuation) all argue price target versus multiple, and I found no published work decomposing the Q1 operating cash flow line items. If the market had done this decomposition, the June 3 reaction would not have been -19.1% on a quarter that beat and raised revenue, the FY27 free-cash-flow guide of 2-4% margin ($18-35M on $879-883M, requiring +$75-92M across Q2-Q4 after -$57.2M in Q1) would not read as implausible to anyone, and the 25-delta skew would not need to be doing the work of expressing it.
findings.independence: ICONIQ partner and Netskope director William Griffith bought ~610,000 shares at a weighted average $11.82 on 2026-07-08 (~$7.2M) and ICONIQ entities added again on 07-10 and 07-13, i.e. an insider with the cash-flow detail buying in size after the print - https://www.fool.com/coverage/filings/2026/07/12/netskope-s-biggest-backer-just-bought-usd7-2-million-in-stock-after-a-steep-selloff/ . Note that the guidance arithmetic and the Q1 line items both trace to the same 2026-06-03 disclosure cluster (release plus 10-Q) and should be collapsed to one source cluster.

findings.finding: Palo Alto Networks reported the identical quarter (ended 2026-07-31) after the close on 2026-09-01 - one session before Netskope - with SASE bookings up 40% year on year and record next-generation-security net new ARR of ~$970M, and its $450M of SASE competitive displacement TCV was described as taken from legacy vendors rather than SSE pure-plays.
findings.why_not_priced: PANW's own shares fell 6.9% on margin and cloud-hosting cost commentary, so the tape narrative out of that print was cost, not SASE demand, and the demand read-across got buried. Netskope has had exactly one session to price it and did not: the sealed baseline shows 5-day run-up of -0.3% and 20-day -2.46%. Had the market applied the read-across, NTSK would have gapped with PANW's SASE line rather than sitting flat, and Zscaler - the other pure-play - does not report until 2026-09-03, so there is no second confirming print in the price yet.
findings.independence: PANW's own results release confirms the same-day report and the July 31 quarter end - https://investors.paloaltonetworks.com/news-releases/news-release-details/palo-alto-networks-announce-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-7 - and the date is independently checkable from the URL path of CNN's coverage, https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/01/palo-alto-networks-panw-q4-2026-earnings.html

findings.finding: Netskope's live job board carries 143 open requisitions of which 67 are sales-facing (30 with 'Sales' in the title, 14 Regional Sales Manager, 28 Solutions Engineer, 9 Channel), 88 of the 143 were updated in August or September 2026, and a Regional Sales Manager req was updated today, 2026-09-02 - the capacity build management staked its second-half net-new-ARR reacceleration on is still being funded, not quietly frozen.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators mis-state this badly - Glassdoor's public page shows 2 open Netskope positions and ZipRecruiter 26, against 143 on the company's own board - so the datum most screens surface implies a hiring stop that does not exist. If the market had the real req count it would not be relying on management's June assertion that half the sales force is ramping; the number is directly observable and updated daily. It also cuts against any hope of a cost-cutting surprise: the opex line stays on its growth path.

findings.finding: Three months after announcing on 2026-06-03 that CFO Drew Del Matto would retire 'effective upon the start of a successor', no successor has been named: EDGAR shows the only 8-K since is a 2026-07-09 item 5.07 annual-meeting filing, and the company's own board carries no CFO, Controller or Chief Accounting Officer requisition.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage treated the retirement as a one-day 2026-06-03 headline and has not revisited the elapsed time. A retiring CFO with no named successor gives the guide tonight - which matters because the disputed line is a cash-flow guide, the softest thing a departing CFO signs off on. This is genuinely two-sided: a successor named alongside results tonight removes an overhang, which is why my band spans zero rather than sitting negative.
findings.independence: The originating 8-K is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002063196/000119312526255439/ck0002063196-20260603.htm - same 2026-06-03 disclosure cluster as finding 1, so this shares a source cluster with it and should not be counted twice.

findings.finding: Netskope's third-party-tracked incident history shows an unusual cluster inside the reported quarter - service impacts at SJC1, SJC2, PVG1/PVG2 and AM2 data centres and to BWAN management plane services in the US region during July 2026, culminating on 2026-07-16 in 'Service Impact to Auth Service and Enterprise browser on all DPs', an authentication failure spanning every data plane.
findings.why_not_priced: Inline-proxy reliability is the one thing an SSE buyer cannot compromise on, and a cross-data-plane auth outage is the kind of event competitors carry into renewal conversations - but status-page history is not aggregated into any financial feed and there is no news coverage of it, so nothing about the price or the coverage would look different either way. I size it near zero deliberately: reliability damage shows up in churn quarters later, not in tonight's ARR, and my confidence in the incident count as anomalous rather than normal for a global proxy network is low.
findings.independence: The SJC1 data-centre incident is separately indexed at https://isdown.app/status/netskope/incidents/620358-service-impact-to-sjc1-data-center , but that is the same tracker, so treat this as a single source with no genuine corroboration.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any registration statement, follow-on, shelf or secondary offering since the 2026-03-17 lock-up expiry - EDGAR shows nothing but Form 4s, two Rule 144 notices in early July, a 5.07 8-K and 13G/As, so there is no fresh supply event queued
Insider Form 4 flow since 2026-07-14 - a seven-week gap consistent with an ordinary blackout, no pre-print selling cluster to find
Acquisition, take-private or activist chatter that would explain the -10.4 point call-bid skew - found only ICONIQ's July open-market buying and Lightspeed's 15.6% 13G/A, nothing strategic
A Zscaler read-across: Zscaler does not report fiscal Q4 until 2026-09-03, the day after Netskope, so the pure-play comparison is not available to either side

Gartner's 2026 SSE Magic Quadrant for evidence of slippage - Netskope is a Leader for a fifth consecutive year and highest in ability to execute in the SASE Platforms quadrant, i.e. no negative competitive signal there
Netskope-specific federal contract awards in the May-July window on SAM.gov - FPDS was decommissioned 2026-02-24 and I could not resolve award-level data for the vendor
Any WARN filing, 8-K item 2.05 or credible dated report of a Netskope restructuring - only undated Glassdoor review text, which I refuse to use
The company's August 2026 community monthly-update changelog and the careers landing page - both truncated on fetch, so no pricing, packaging or deprecation change could be confirmed
A CFO successor announcement anywhere in press releases, 8-Ks or the leadership page
baseline_tension: My two real findings both point the same way as the baseline's unusual call-bid skew (-10.4 vol points, put/call OI 0.48) and the +28% recovery off the June low, which means the market has largely got there ahead of me; the only thing cutting the other way is the company's own 0-for-3 print record at a median -19%, and that is already stated in the baseline rather than discovered by me, so I hold the number close to zero.
